 :Judgment:

This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.12,00,000/ for the injuries sustained in the Road Traffic accident.
2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:

That on 02012020 in between 9.30 a.m. to 10.00 a.m., when the Petitioner was riding his Honda Activa bearing No.KA 02EP5097 from Rajendranagar towards N.G.V block gate on the extreme left side on Koramangala 80 Feet Road, Bangalore,
at that time, one motor cycle bearing Regn. No.KA03AH8659 ridden by its rider came in a rash and negligent manner, came from behind and dashed to the Petitioner's Honda Activa and caused the accident.
Due to the said accident, the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries to all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was shifted to Health India Hospital wherein first aid treatment was taken and thereafter he was shifted to Bowring and Lady Curzon hospital, wherein he was admitted as an inpatient.
He has spent more than Rs.50,000/ towards medical expenses and other incidental expenses.
Prior to the accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was doing coolie and was earning Rs.700/ per day.
Due to the accident, he has sustained grievous injuries causing permanent disablement.

The Respondent No.1 is the owner and the Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle and therefore, both Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.
3. In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondents, Respondent No.1 and 2 appeared before the Court through their respective Counsels and filed their Objection Statements.

Respondent No.1 has filed his Objection Statement to the main Petition and contended that,
Respondent No.1 is a Company interalia is engaged in the business of providing self drive motor cycle rental, nonmotorized vehicle sharing or a two wheeler sharing services under its brand "Bounce" to customers registered on its software application available on iOS and Android operating systems.

He further contended that, the Respondent No.1's bikes are also rented by various delivery Shanthaveeraiah vs M/S.Wickedride Adventure on 17 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88639336/
2 agencies like Big Basket, Dunzo, Amazon, Swiggy etc.,
Further he contended that, he has received a request for booking TVS Scooter Zest bearing No.KA03AH8659 from one Mohan Charan Sahoo through his registered mobile number.
His request was processed upon verifying the validity of his driving license.

Further he contended that, on 17.01.2020 the Sub inspector of Police at Adugodi Traffic Police station issued a notice U/s 133 of MV Act and then he gained knowledge about the accident and he submitted the records before the concerned police station. Thereafter, the I.O has filed Charge sheet against the Santhosh Kumar Behera who was riding the vehicle at the time of the accident and he was having a valid driving license at the time of the accident.
Further contended that, after booking the vehicle Mr. Mohan Charan Sahoo has given the vehicle to Mr. Santhosh Kumar Behera.

Further he denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also the accident caused by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle and the also the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in the said accident and expenses incurred for the medical treatment.
Further he contended that, the vehicle was insured with the 2nd Respondent and as on the date of the accident, the policy is valid.
On these and other grounds the Respondent No.1 has prayed to dismiss the Petition against him.

Respondent No.2 filed Objections to the main petition and denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending motor cycle.
Further, it has admitted the policy.
Further it has denied the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in the accident and the expenses incurred for the medical treatment.
On these grounds, Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.
4. On the basis of the above pleadings, my learned predecessor has framed the following Issues.
ISSUES 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that he sustained grievous injuries in the nature of permanent disablement on 02.01.2020 at about 9.30 a.m. to 10.00 a.m. near Amul office, on Koramangala 80 feet road, Koramangala, Bengaluru, in an accident arising due to rash and negligent riding of rider of Scooter bearing No.KA03AH 8659?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If so, what amount and from whom?
3 . What Order or Award ?
5. In order to substantiate the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 9 documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.9.
He also got examined one witness as P.W.2 and got marked 4 documents as per Ex.P.10 to P.13 and closed his side evidence.
On the other hand, the Respondents did not choose to lead any oral or documentary evidence.

6. Having heard the arguments of the learned Counsel for the Petitioner and the learned Counsel for the Respondents and upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Shanthaveeraiah vs M/S.Wickedride Adventure on 17 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88639336/
3  Issue No. 2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No. 3 : As per the Final Order
for the following :

REASONS 7. Issue No. 1 : It is the case of the Petitioner that he had sustained grievous injuries in the Motor Vehicle accident that occurred on 02012020 at about 09.30 a.m. to 10.00 a.m. ,due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Scooter bearing Regn.No.KA03AH8659.
8. On the other hand, the Respondents have denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle.
9. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, he got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 9 documents as Ex.P.1 to P.9.
He also examined one witness as P.W.2 and got marked 4 documents as per Ex.P10 to Ex.P13.
P.W.1 has re iterated the Petition averments in his chiefaffidavit.
Ex.P1 to Ex.P5 are the True copies of FIR with Complaint, Spot Panchanama along with sketch, IMV report, Wound certificate and Chargesheet.
Ex.P.6 is the Discharge cum ID card.
Ex.P.7 is the Medical bills.
Ex.P.8 is the Prescriptions.
Ex.P.9 is the Aadhar card.

10. Upon going through Ex.P1, it shows that on the complaint lodged by Revannaiah before Adugodi Police Station, the ASI of the concerned Police Station has registered the case against the rider of the Scooter bearing Reg.No.No.KA03AH 8659 for the offences punishable under sec.
279, 337 of IPC and U/s 134(A&B) and 187 of IMV Act.
Ex.P2 is the Spot panchanama along with sketch which shows that the concerned police had drawn mahazar at the spot in the presence of panchas.
Ex.P3 is the IMV report which shows that the accident does not occurred due to any mechanical defect of the vehicles.
Ex.P.4 is the Wound Certificate of the Petitioner which shows that the Petitioner had sustained the grievous injuries.

Ex.P5 is the Charge sheet which shows that after thorough investigation, the PSI of Adugodi Traffic Police Station has submitted Chargesheet against the rider of the offending motor cycle for the offences punishable under Sec. 279, 338 of IPC and U/s 134(A&B) and 187 of IMV Act.

11. Upon going through the Chargesheet i.e., Ex.P5 Column No.17 reads as under:
" 02012020   9.30  10.00     .12

Shanthaveeraiah vs M/S.Wickedride Adventure on 17 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88639336/
4 01
Ex.P6 is the Discharge card which shows that the Petitioner was admitted in Bowring and Lady Curzon hospital as an inpatient from 02012020 to 13012020.
Ex.P.7 is the Medical bills and Ex.P.8 is the Prescriptions.
13. Further, P.W.1 examined Dr.Somashekhar as P.W.2 and they also reiterated about the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a RTA.
14. To rebut the evidence of P.W.1, the Learned Counsel for Respondent No.2 has cross examined the P.W.1.
But nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the testimony of the petitioner.

15. Though the Respondents had taken contention that the accident does not caused due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle, they did not choose to lead any evidence to substantiate their contentions.
Moreover, after thorough investigation, the I.O. has filed Charge sheet against the rider of the offending vehicle.

Therefore, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident is caused by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle and in the said accident, the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the 'Affirmative'.
16. Issue No. 2 :
As the petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
17. In the petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 41 years.

Further, in the Aadhar card i.e.,
Ex.P9, the date of birth of the Petitioner was shown as 01011975.
The accident taken place on 02012020.

Hence, the age of the Petitioner, as on the date of accident was 45 years and the same is to be taken for consideration.
18.
Further, the petitioner has averred that he was doing coolie and was earning Rs.700/ per day.
In this regard, he has not produced any documents to prove the income.

Therefore, in the absence of income proof, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, since the accident has been occurred in the year 2020, the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority i.e. 14,500/ p.m. for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
19. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING:
20.

The Wound Certificate i.e., Ex.P4 and other medical records reveals that in the accident the petitioner has sustained following injuries:
Shanthaveeraiah vs M/S.Wickedride Adventure on 17 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88639336/
5

1. Abrasions over bleeding to medial malleolous 2 x 1 cm. lef leg.
2. Abrasion 3 x 1 cm. over anterior aspect of left leg.
Mid 1/3rd deformity.
Xray reveals left closed distal 1/3rd both bone left fracture.
Further, the Doctor has opined that said injury No.1 is simple in nature and injury No.2 is grievous in nature.
Further, P.W.2 has also reiterated about the grievous injuries sustained by the Petitioner.
21. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that,
awarding compensation of Rs.30,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.

II COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES :
22.
Bearing in mind the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.30,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.

III COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID -UP PERIOD:
23.
The petitioner has averred in the petition as well as in his evidence that he was admitted as an inpatient in Bowring and Lady Curzon hospital as an inpatient from 02012020 to 13012020.
P.W.2 Dr.Ramesh.B has also reiterated the same in his evidence.
24. Upon going through Ex.P6 Discharge card which shows that the Petitioner was admitted in Bowring and Lady Curzon hospital as an inpatient from 02012020 to 1301 2020 i.e., for 12 days.
The total period which the petitioner was admitted as inpatient is 12 days.
25. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that the laid up period may be considered as tree months.
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.43,500/ under this head (@ Rs.14,500/ per month ).

IV COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :
26.

Admittedly, the petitioner has sustained injuries and during the laid up period, the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also he might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for his conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of Rs.9,000/ (@ Rs.100/ per day) towards attendants charges, Rs.9,000/
towards extra diet and nourishment and Rs.9,000/ towards conveyance would be just and Shanthaveeraiah vs M/S.Wickedride Adventure on 17 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88639336/
6 reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.27,000/ under this head.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENCES :
27. The Petitioner has deposed that he has spent Rs.50,000/ towards medical expenses.
In order to prove this fact, he has produced 14 medical bills which totally marked at Ex.P.7 which totally amounting to Rs.6,266/.
I have gone through the said medical bills.
Upon going through the said medical bills, the total of acceptable medical bills comes to Rs. 5,861/.
Hence, by rounding off the same, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.5,900/ as a compensation under this head.
VI COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS/COMPENSATION
TOWARDS
PERMANENT DISABILITY :
28 . The Petitioner has alleged that due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident, he has suffered permanent disablement and he is not able to do his work as he used to do earlier.
Even in his evidence, P.W.1 has deposed to that effect.
Further, the Petitioner got examined doctor by name Dr.S.A.Somashekara as P.W.2 who also deposed regarding the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a road traffic accident.
Further, he got marked OPD record, Case sheet, two Xrays at Ex.P.10 to Ex.P.13.
He assessed permanent physical disability of the left lower limb at 38% and whole body physical disability at 19%.
In the cross examination, he deposed that he is not a treated doctor.
He admitted that the fractures are united.
He has denied the suggestions putforth to him by the Learned Counsel for Respondent No.2.

Hence, having regard to the medical records placed on record and evidence of P.W.2 and the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner, I am of the opinion that considering the disability of the petitioner with respect to the whole body at 10% would be just and proper.
As per Sarla Verma's Case (2009 ACJ 1298 SC), the multiplier applicable to the Petitioner is 14.

With multiplier of 14, income of Rs.14,500/ per month and disability of the Petitioner with respect to his whole body at 10%, the loss of future income comes to Rs.2,43,600/ (Rs.14,500/ x 12 =
1,74,000/, Rs.1,74,000/x 14 x 10/100 = Rs.2,43,600/).
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,43,600/ under this head.

TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
29.

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering Rs. 30,000/
2. Loss of amenities Rs. 30,000/
Shanthaveeraiah vs M/S.Wickedride Adventure on 17 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88639336/
7 3.
Attendant's charges, Extra Rs. 27,000/ diet, and conveyance 4.

Medical expenses Rs. 5,900/
5. Loss of income during the Rs. 43,500/ laid up period
6. Loss of Future income Rs.2,43,600/ Total Rs.3,80,000/
Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.3,80,000/ with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

30. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent riding on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle bearing No.No.KA 03AH8659.
There is no dispute about the validity of the policy.
Moreover, Respondent No.2 did not choose to lead evidence to prove its contention.
Therefore, both Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
31. Point No. 3 : In view of my findings on Points No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondent No. 1 and 2 U/Sec. 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for Compensation of Rs.3,80,000/ along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the Insurer of the offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.

On deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.2, 75% of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner by way of E payment and after proper identification and the remaining 25% of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in his name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years of his choice.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs. 1000/.
Draw Award accordingly.
